All hardcode the VM layout /home/ubuntu/systems/trading-system with the interpreter /home/ubuntu/systems/venv/bin/python; five run as User=ubuntu, token-watcher runs as User=root. A push to main force-checkouts over the live tree (`checkout -f`), silently discarding any uncommitted edit made on the VM. Nothing in the hook reports what was discarded.
`crontab <file>` replaces the pushing user's ENTIRE crontab, so any entry added on the VM outside the canonical file is deleted by the next push.

The crontab-integrity gate runs AFTER the checkout (line 31), and on mismatch it only echoes a WARNING and falls through to 'Deployment complete.' (line 39) - leaving new code with the previous crontab. Git also ignores post-receive's exit status, so nothing can fail the push at that point.

The market-hours deploy guard and the cron-canonical equality/blast-radius guard live in pre-receive, which this file states is NOT installed by default; unless it has been manually armed in the bare repo, neither guard is in the live push path. The guard additionally fails OPEN when market_hours_guard.sh is unreadable (lines 41, 45-46) and on an unparseable clock (market_hours_guard.sh:37-38).
pre-receive builds `rm -rf` from a shell variable in a trap, and again at lines 51 and 77; if $TMP were ever empty the expansion would target the caller's tree.

install_vm_services.sh copies only trading-system, token-watcher and alert-watcher (lines 18-20). No script anywhere in deploy/ or scripts/ installs security-watcher.service, trading-watchman.service or cron-watchdog.{service,timer} - yet the auditd rules watch /etc/systemd/system/security-watcher.service (deploy/security/trading-security.rules:25) as if it were installed.

With `set -euo pipefail` (line 12), a failure of `netfilter-persistent save` (line 47) aborts the script after the units have already been copied and enabled but BEFORE token-watcher is restarted (line 50) - a partial install that prints no summary.

alert-watcher.service is enabled for boot at line 31 while the closing message tells the operator to start it manually - an enabled-but-not-started unit whose state differs between now and the next reboot.

The PC starter waits 15 seconds and then asserts `systemctl is-active trading-system` (lines 81-82, exit 1 at line 90), while the watcher that performs the start polls every 30 seconds (token-watcher.service:11 `Environment=SLEEP_SEC=30`) - so a healthy boot can report a hard failure.

zerodha_morning.ps1 scp's the token directly onto its final filename (and zerodha_morning.bat:57 does the same), bypassing the two-phase .tmp+ssh-mv copy that scripts/copy_token_to_vm.bat:19,:34 exists to provide; token_watcher.sh:129 only defers when a `.tmp` file is present, which this path never creates.

The header forbids enabling `rotate` (line 10, because it would race the Python RotatingFileHandler) while the stanza itself declares `daily` (line 19) with `rotate 0` (line 23). Declared intent and declared directives disagree.

README describes claude heartbeat cron lines in deploy/cron/trading-system.cron and a 'PERSONAL TOOLING section' (line 20). No line of that 151-line file matches 'claude' (grep returns nothing), config/cron_registry.yaml contains no `personal_tooling: true` job, and the `claude_cd` env_wrapper defined at scripts/generate_crontab.py:52 is used by no job - so the restore recipe at lines 17-21 restores no heartbeat, and the personal_tooling WARN-vs-CRITICAL branch in scripts/check_cron_drift.py:89 is unreachable.

The watchdog docstring says exit 0 means 'both ran (or non-trading day)' but the check excludes only Saturday/Sunday (line 38: today.weekday() >= 5); an NSE weekday holiday is treated as a market day, so a missing heartbeat on a holiday writes a CRITICAL sentinel. No holiday calendar is consulted in this file.

trading-watchman.service declares BindsTo=trading-system.service (line 4) and also WantedBy=multi-user.target (line 34), i.e. it is enabled to start at boot while bound to a unit that the boot path does not start (trading-system is started only by token_watcher.sh when a fresh token lands). Recorded as declared; the resulting systemd state was not observed.
token_watcher.sh keeps its crash-restart counter and its once-per-day alert flags in /tmp, so a reboot silently resets the 3/hour crash backoff and re-arms the HALT/startup-failure alerts.

Derived defaults instead of required fields: effective_heartbeat_required = monitored unless overridden (:132-135); effective_detection_method = explicit, else heartbeat_db when heartbeat-required, else exit_code_file (:137-147); effective_category from cadence via resolve_category (:57-62, :127-129).

HOW DRIFT IS DETECTED, AND WHAT IT COMPARES. scripts/check_cron_drift.py runs two independent passes (docstring :5-19); the cron entry point _cron_main (:226-240) first calls skip_if_non_trading_day("check_cron_drift") and returns 0 on a non-trading day, so PASS 1/2 only run on trading days unless main() is invoked by hand. PASS 1 (signal-miss, :57-80): the expected set is registry.expected_heartbeat_jobs(today, before_time=now.time()) (:70-71), i.e. monitored jobs due today whose `schedule`-derived due_time is <= now, with jobs having no parseable due_time (intraday/hourly) always included (core/cron_registry.py:290-309). For each expected job it dispatches on effective_detection_method: exit_code_file -> _read_marker(j.marker_name or j.name, ...) (:74-77) reading data_store/cron_marks/<name>.done, whose content is "<rc> <iso-ts>" and whose timestamp prefix must equal today (cron_officer.py:359-371); anything else -> the job NAME must appear among store.get_cron_heartbeats_since(now-24h) (:68-69, :78-79). PASS 2 (content drift, :103-129): load_jobs(registry_path) returns raw dicts (generate_crontab.py:313-320), enabled-only (:107), each composed into one canonical crontab line (:109); the live text comes from `crontab -l` or --crontab-file (:132-140); each live command line (blank, '#' and 'SHELL=' lines skipped, generate_crontab.py:137-144) is normalized by parse()->compose() (:116) and, if resolve_job_name() of the parsed fields is not a registry key, listed as unregistered/RAN_UNVERIFIED (:118-119); a live line that fails parse/compose is unparseable (:120-121); any generated line absent from the normalized live set is absent_warn when personal_tooling else absent_critical (:123-128). The comparison is set-based, so line ORDER is ignored (:104-105). What the composed line actually contains — i.e. the ONLY fields drift compares, byte-exactly — is cron_expression + the env_wrapper prefix + command + optional " <log_target>" + optional marker block (generate_crontab.py:72-88, prefixes at :48-53, marker text at :67-69). Not compared at all: script, schedule, type, critical, market_day_only, cadence, monitored, category, detection_method, excluded_reason, weekday, day_of_month; personal_tooling only downgrades an absence from CRITICAL to WARN (:126-127). Severity (:143-170): CRITICAL if absent_critical or unparseable (:95, :147-148), WARNING if PASS-1 misses or any other drift (:149-150), else the OK string at :169; exit code is 0 only on OK (:223); non-OK sends Telegram unless --dry-run (:203-208); the checker records its own heartbeat last (:216-221). The Cron Officer reuses the same PASS 2 inside its EOD "ROSTER INTEGRITY" block (a) (cron_officer.py:629-641) and adds auto-discovery of live-not-registry lines as RAN_UNVERIFIED (:563-585), plus a watcher check (d) that cron_officer_eod and check_cron_drift both heartbeated today (:666-673). cron_officer.py also has an OLDER, weaker diff, build_change_report (:310-340), which token-matches only python jobs by script basename (:273-281) and compares HH:MM parsed from the live line against `schedule`-derived due_time (:325-327).

WHAT THE REGISTRY DOES NOT CONTROL. (1) It does not install anything: in all four files the only crontab invocations are reads — `crontab -l` at cron_officer.py:557, cron_officer.py:890 and check_cron_drift.py:136; generate_crontab writes the canonical text only to stdout or --out (:386-395). Editing `enabled` or a time changes generation and drift verdicts, not the live crontab. (2) The host-specific strings are hardcoded constants, not registry data: PROJ, VENV_PY, CLAUDE_DIR, MARKS, SHELL_LINE (generate_crontab.py:42-46) and the four env prefixes (:48-53) — a job can only pick one of none|python|python_nopath|claude_cd (:54), not its own interpreter or directory. (3) The marker-writing shell fragment and marks directory (:45, :67-69) and the canonical header plus the SHELL=/bin/bash line (:46, :177-189) are fixed text. (4) When a job actually fires is `cron_expression` alone (:81); `schedule` is documentation (yaml:4-5, generate_crontab.py:17) yet it is the ONLY field the Officer's timing logic reads — due_time parses the leading HH:MM of `schedule` (core/cron_registry.py:36, :115-124) and drives PENDING/MISSED (cron_officer.py:404-416) and last_due_time/eod_report_time (core:268-288). Nothing in these files compares `schedule` with `cron_expression`. (5) The EOD fire time is not computed from the registry at run time: eod_report_time() (core:279-288) is used only for a simulated --as-of-date run (cron_officer.py:939-940); the real firing is the literal "50 18 * * 1-5" at yaml:709. (6) Holiday skipping is not imposed by the registry: the generated lines carry only day-of-week fields, cadence only shapes the Officer's/drift-checker's expectations (core:253-266, holiday lookup with a weekday<5 fallback at :179-187), and the actual skip is each job's own (e.g. check_cron_drift.py:236-240). (7) Alert routing, thresholds and grace behaviour are code: severity maps at check_cron_drift.py:143-151 and cron_officer.py:429-434; the registry supplies only the officer block's times, eod_gap_minutes, miss_grace_minutes and telegram_ban_until (yaml:757-767, model core:150-167). (8) No service/process management appears anywhere in these files: grep for systemd/systemctl/.service hits only two comments (check_cron_drift.py:21, :214). (9) bootstrap/gate_check in generate_crontab.py (:191-204, :249-298, :335-357) are one-time migration paths, and _SPECIAL_NAME (:198-204) plus the db_retention special case (:221-222) are hardcoded name-resolution rules the registry cannot change.

defects.what: Marker lookup disagrees between the two consumers: the Cron Officer reads the marker by job.name, while the drift-checker reads it by (marker_name or name). db_retention_vacuum declares marker_name: db_retention (config/cron_registry.yaml:154) and its generated line therefore writes cron_marks/db_retention.done, so the Officer's lookup of cron_marks/db_retention_vacuum.done can never find a file and that job is permanently NO_SIGNAL (which never escalates, cron_officer.py:429-434).

db_retention and db_retention_vacuum share one marker file (marker_name: db_retention at lines 139 and 154) while db_retention is cadence:daily (line 131) so is_due_on returns True on Sunday (core/cron_registry.py:255-256) even though its cron_expression '30 2 * * 1-6' excludes Sunday: on a Sunday the Officer credits db_retention as COMPLETED from the marker the vacuum line wrote.

is_due_on/jobs_due_on never consult `enabled`, so the disabled job daily_report (enabled:false at config/cron_registry.yaml:550) is still listed as due today by the briefing (scripts/cron_officer.py:118) and the EOD report (scripts/cron_officer.py:690) even though generation omits it (scripts/generate_crontab.py:327-328) and content_drift filters it out (scripts/check_cron_drift.py:107).

liveness_probe is monitored:false (line 352) and declares no marker_name, so its effective_detection_method resolves to exit_code_file (core/cron_registry.py:143-147) and the Officer reads cron_marks/liveness_probe.done -- a file its composed cron line never writes, because compose() only appends the marker block when marker_name is set (scripts/generate_crontab.py:85-87). The job therefore reads NO_SIGNAL every day.

content_drift calls compose() for every enabled job inside a dict comprehension that is not wrapped in try/except, while compose() raises ValueError on an unknown env_wrapper or a missing cron_expression/command (scripts/generate_crontab.py:76, :80). One malformed enabled job would abort PASS 2 and propagate out of main() (no except around line 195), skipping both the alert and the self-heartbeat at lines 216-221. All 47 current jobs do declare cron_expression, command and env_wrapper.

When `crontab -l` cannot be read, _read_crontab returns None (line 140) and cd stays None (line 195), so PASS 2 never runs -- yet if PASS 1 finds nothing the reported OK line still asserts 'live == registry'. That claim is an output string, not a verified comparison.

market_day_only is declared on all 47 jobs but is read by no scheduling logic in the consuming code: it appears only as the model field, in a comment, and in the one-time bootstrap metadata list (scripts/generate_crontab.py:192). Due-ness is decided by `cadence` alone (core/cron_registry.py:253-263), as the drift-checker's own note at scripts/check_cron_drift.py:229 states.

summary: One file is the whole session: `data_store/session/zerodha_token.json`. Cron deletes it at 05:00 every day, cron re-mints it at 08:15 Mon-Fri via a headless password+TOTP login (`scripts/auto_refresh_token.py`), and a root-owned systemd poll loop (`deploy/token_watcher.sh`, every 30 s) is the ONLY component in this tree that automatically issues `systemctl start trading-system.service` — it does so when the token's `date` field equals today (IST) and the IST hour is in [8,16). Nothing in the crontab starts the service. At runtime `main.py` reads the same file twice: once early (:2370) to inject `ZERODHA_API_KEY`/`ZERODHA_ACCESS_TOKEN` into the environment for `KiteConnect`, and once at the account gate (:2555) via `zerodha_login.is_token_valid` (account_id + date + non-empty access_token) which returns exit 6 on failure. The PC-side scripts (`deploy/zerodha_morning.ps1`/`.bat`) are a manual alternative path: interactive browser login then scp to the VM. Three independent, non-agreeing staleness definitions exist (JSON `date` field; POSIX mtime; Windows LastWriteTime), and the `expires_at` value written into the token is enforced by nothing. Two defects found by reading: the missing-token branch in main.py is unreachable dead code (a missing file yields TypeError -> exit 2, not the intended exit 6), and the module docstring's declared refresh time (08:00) contradicts the registry and crontab (08:15). Nothing was written or changed; this tree has no `data_store/session/` directory.

defects.what: DEAD ERROR PATH: main.py's missing-token branch is unreachable. `except FileNotFoundError:` (main.py:2372) guards a try block whose only statements are AccountRegistry.load (which converts FileNotFoundError into ConfigMissingError at core/account_registry.py:173-177, and ConfigMissingError derives from TradingSystemError/Exception per core/exceptions.py:30,56,69 -- NOT from FileNotFoundError), primary(), an os.environ lookup, load_token (which swallows OSError and returns None, scripts/zerodha_login.py:56-57) and a subscript. So with the token file absent in live mode, main.py:2371 raises TypeError on None, which reaches only the catch-all at main.py:4327 and exits 2 -- never the intended `return 6` at main.py:2378, and the CRITICAL 'Token file missing. Run: python scripts/zerodha_login.py' at main.py:2373-2376 is never printed for a missing token file.

DECLARED-TIME CONTRADICTION inside one file: the module docstring says the job 'Runs daily at 08:00 IST Mon-Fri via cron', while the same file's _cron_main docstring (line 405) says '08:15 TOTP refresh', and both the registry (config/cron_registry.yaml:200,208) and the generated crontab (deploy/cron/trading-system.cron:52) declare 08:15 / '15 8 * * 1-5'. The docstring is the outlier.

THREE NON-AGREEING STALENESS DEFINITIONS for the same file: (a) the JSON `date` field -- scripts/zerodha_login.py:75 (the authoritative gate) and deploy/token_watcher.sh:65 (the starter); (b) POSIX mtime -- scripts/preflight/checks/broker.py:193-196 via _file_mdate (broker.py:76-80); (c) Windows LastWriteTime -- deploy/zerodha_morning.ps1:43, whose .bat sibling uses (a) instead (deploy/zerodha_morning.bat:35). A file copied or touched after minting is 'fresh' to (b)/(c) and can be stale to (a), and vice versa.

WRITE-ONLY FIELD: `expires_at` is computed and stored in every token (next 05:00 IST, scripts/zerodha_login.py:153-155, :164) but no gate consults it. Measured over every non-docs/non-test .py in the tree, the only reader is scripts/healthcheck_server.py:44, which merely echoes it in the payload -- the `ok` verdict on line 43 ignores it. (scripts/copy_gate.py:124 and scripts/security_monitor.py:604 read an expires_at belonging to a different, COPY_TOKEN_ISSUED, token.)

THE STARTER AND THE GATE DISAGREE ON ACCOUNT: token_watcher.sh's token_is_fresh checks only `date` and non-empty access_token -- it never compares account_id, which is_token_valid does require (scripts/zerodha_login.py:74). A token minted for a non-primary account therefore satisfies the watcher and triggers `systemctl start` (deploy/token_watcher.sh:186), after which main.py:2555 rejects it and returns exit 6. Exit 6 is absent from RestartPreventExitStatus=3 4 5 (deploy/systemd/trading-system.service:35) while Restart=on-failure/RestartSec=10 (:33-34) apply, so systemd restarts it; the watcher's own catch-all branch (deploy/token_watcher.sh:168) also treats 6 as a crash.

THE MORNING SCRIPTS BYPASS THE ATOMIC COPY THEY EXIST ALONGSIDE: zerodha_morning.ps1 scps straight onto the final filename ($VMTokenDest is the destination DIRECTORY, ps1:18), and zerodha_morning.bat:57 does the same. scripts/copy_token_to_vm.bat:5-7,17-34 documents and implements the two-phase .tmp + ssh mv precisely so the watcher cannot read a partially written file, and deploy/token_watcher.sh:129 only skips on a `.tmp` sibling -- which a direct scp never creates.

WAIT SHORTER THAN THE POLL INTERVAL: the morning script sleeps 15 s before asserting the service is active, but the watcher polls every 30 s (SLEEP_SEC=30 in deploy/systemd/token-watcher.service:11, default at deploy/token_watcher.sh:22). The 'service is NOT active' error at deploy/zerodha_morning.ps1:82-90 (and .bat:71-81) can therefore fire on a perfectly healthy chain. Same 15 s in deploy/zerodha_morning.bat:67.

UNDECLARED REQUIRED SECRETS: the headless refresh requires user_id and password (scripts/auto_refresh_token.py:349, :350) and returns exit 1 when either is absent (:359-367), but .env.example -- read in full, 50 lines -- declares no ZERODHA_USER_ID* or ZERODHA_PASSWORD* key anywhere; it lists only API_KEY/API_SECRET/TOTP per account (lines 16-39) plus Telegram and WEBHOOK_SECRET.

INTERPRETER INCONSISTENCY in the preflight auto-fix: it spawns bare 'python' with no cwd and no PYTHONPATH, whereas every cron invocation of the same script uses the absolute venv interpreter with PYTHONPATH=. (deploy/cron/trading-system.cron:52, and :58 for the orchestrator that calls this fix). Whether bare 'python' resolves on the VM's cron PATH is UNKNOWN from this tree.

START-WINDOW MISMATCH between the starter and the process it starts: token_watcher.sh will only start the service while the IST hour is in [8,16) (deploy/token_watcher.sh:50), but main.py's own START window is [08:00, 18:15) (main.py:2008-2009, :2023; SERVICE_WINDOW_END_MAX = 18:15 at core/config_loader.py:83). Between 16:00 and 18:15 no automatic start can occur even though main.py would permit one -- and main.py:2181-2182 tells the reader that 'Token-watcher starts the service in-window'.

label: boot:shutdown-eod
summary:
Two distinct mechanisms, read as code in D:/Projects/wt-sr-shadow-15sep.

(A) EOD SQUARE-OFF (orders/eod_squareoff.py) — a polled, once-per-date sequence. A daemon thread (main.py:4129-4135) calls EodSquareoff.check_and_fire(now_ist()) every `eod_squareoff.poll_interval_sec` (5). It fires when now.time() >= trading_hours.eod_squareoff_time ("15:17", system_config.yaml:49; compared at core/market_windows.py:205), on a non-holiday, and only once per IST date (_fired_for_date claim, eod_squareoff.py:222/227). The fire sequence is: clear gate state (dead — entry_gate is never wired) -> clear parked retest candidates -> write an IN_PROGRESS row to eod_squareoff_log -> soft_kill("EOD_SQUAREOFF") -> PASS 1 cancel pending intraday ENTRY orders and pending SL/TGT legs -> sleep 2s -> PASS 2 exit open positions -> LIMIT->MARKET promotion after limit_grace_sec (120) -> residual broker-position sweep -> stale-order sweep -> summary log -> eod_squareoff_log COMPLETE -> WAL checkpoint(TRUNCATE) -> publish EodSquareoffComplete -> fund_manager.reset_daily_pnl() -> resume kill switch if this module set it -> Telegram DAILY SUMMARY.

Per product: DELIVERY/CNC is never touched (docstring EOD6 at eod_squareoff.py:23/34; every DB query filters `product IN ('MIS','CO')`, state_store.py:1036/1163/1246; the broker snapshot filters on core.constants.EMERGENCY_FLATTEN_PRODUCTS = {MIS, CO}). CO (order_protocol=='CO_PLUS_TGT' and entry variety=='co') is closed by cancelling the CO bracket, not by a reverse order. MIS / LIMIT_TRIPLE gets an aggressive LIMIT at LTP∓limit_aggressive_pct (0.01) when exit_protocol=="LIMIT_THEN_MARKET", falling back to MARKET per-symbol when no LTP, then unfilled LIMITs are cancelled and re-placed as MARKET after the grace window.

(B) PROCESS SHUTDOWN (main.py). Nothing in the EOD fire stops the process. The service self-exits only via the eod-self-exit daemon (main.py:1329-1563), which waits for trading_hours.service_window_end ("17:35", system_config.yaml:112) and then sets _shutdown_event once no open position REQUIRES this service; a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler (main.py:1573) is the other setter. main() wakes at main.py:4284 and calls _shutdown(...) at main.py:4287. _shutdown drains a HARD_KILL flatten, emits the effect census, stops every worker in reverse order, cancels pending ENTRY orders (SL/TGT/EOD legs are deliberately left at the broker), sends a Telegram "System Stopping", writes a SHUTDOWN row to system_events, runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE), closes the store, and logs the final line.

THE FINAL LOG LINE is `_log.info("Shutdown complete")` at main.py:1839 — the only occurrence in the tree (a repo-wide grep over .py/.sh/.ps1/.service/.md finds no other writer). It is a LOG string, not a DB row.

Shutdown does NOT complete when: (1) the self-exit gate never says "due" — before window_end, a HARD_KILL flatten in progress (or the flatten probe raising), a position-count error, or any position classified as requiring this service (an INTRADAY survivor, an identity CONFLICT/UNRESOLVED, or a DELIVERY position whose ENTRY product is not CNC); (2) the self-exit thread was never armed (--interactive / --resume / TS_IGNORE_MARKET_WINDOW=1, main.py:4164-4168); (3) an exception anywhere in _main_locked after start-up — _shutdown() at main.py:4287 is NOT inside a try/finally, so the handlers at main.py:4324-4329 exit 1/2 and "Shutdown complete" is never written; (4) systemd SIGKILLs at TimeoutStopSec=30 (deploy/systemd/trading-system.service:25). Inside _shutdown itself every teardown step is individually wrapped, so a failing worker still reaches line 1839; a flatten that outlives the 15s grace only produces a CRITICAL (main.py:1647-1653) and shutdown continues.

defects.what: The FIX-046 'clear gate state at EOD' step is unreachable in this wiring. EodSquareoff's ctor parameter `entry_gate` defaults to None (orders/eod_squareoff.py:132) and the construction in main.py (lines 3310-3329) never passes it, nor is there a setter for it (only set_retest_monitor and set_stale_order_sweep exist). So `self._entry_gate is not None` is always False and the log line 'FIX-046: cleared N gate entries at EOD' (eod_squareoff.py:344) can never be emitted. Recorded only.

Product-filter asymmetry in the phase-2 promotion sweep. The top-of-fire broker snapshot filters to MIS/CO (eod_squareoff.py:1086) precisely so a delivery position's qty is never used; the phase-2 re-fetch builds `current_qty` with no product filter at all (only `int(p.qty) != 0`). A CNC/delivery position in the same symbol therefore makes `remaining` non-zero, and the promoted order is placed for `qty=remaining` (line 1666) with intent="INTRADAY". Recorded only.

Dead config knob: eod_squareoff.auto_resume_kill_switch exists in the YAML (config/system_config.yaml:362) and in the schema (core/config_loader.py:669) but is never passed to EodSquareoff (ctor call main.py:3310-3329), and the resume is unconditional on `_we_set_soft_kill`. Setting it false would change nothing. Recorded only.

The injected time authority is stored and never used. The ctor documents `time_authority: object,  # module with now_ist(); injected for testability` (eod_squareoff.py:119) and assigns self._ta here, but a repo-wide grep of the file shows `_ta` appears on this line only; every timestamp in the fire path uses the module-level `now_ist` imported at eod_squareoff.py:63 (e.g. :334, :463, :895, :1215, :1469, :1746). Recorded only.

The residual-sweep exit writes no orders row. _place_marketable_limit_exit places the order and calls order_monitor.track, but unlike every other exit path (:1226, :1336, :1686) it performs no INSERT into orders, so an EOD_RESIDUAL flatten has no local order record. Recorded only.

_shutdown() is not protected by try/finally. Any exception raised in _main_locked after the subsystems start (for example effect_telemetry.assert_composition re-raising at main.py:4281) skips the whole teardown: no flatten drain, no SHUTDOWN system_events row, no WAL checkpoint, no store.close, and no 'Shutdown complete' line. The process exits 1 or 2 via the handlers at main.py:4324-4329 (and with Restart=on-failure, systemd restarts it). Recorded only.

The FIX-088 ticker-thread guard is inert at the EOD call site. StateStore.checkpoint's guard only runs when a live_feed is supplied (`if live_feed is not None:`, core/state_store.py:300), and eod_squareoff.py:501 calls `self._store.checkpoint()` with no argument, so the TRUNCATE pragma is always issued from that site. (In practice the fire runs on the 'eod_squareoff_poll' thread, not the ticker thread.) Recorded only.

paper_live:
Mode does not branch anywhere in orders/eod_squareoff.py or in main.py's shutdown/EOD path — the whole difference sits at the broker I/O boundary inside ZerodhaAdapter, plus the alert-title label.

1. Cancels cannot fail in paper. ZerodhaAdapter.cancel_order returns CancelResult(success=True) unconditionally in paper (broker/zerodha_adapter.py:1043-1049), so cancels_failed is structurally 0 and the CRITICAL paths at eod_squareoff.py:887 and :986 are unreachable. In live, a kite rejection returns success=False with a reason (zerodha_adapter.py:1068-1074) and the row counts as failed.

2. Positions come from the in-process paper book. get_positions in paper returns from _paper_positions with signed qty and product defaulted to "" (broker/zerodha_adapter.py:1229-1257); in live it reads kite's "net" list (:1276-1288). The comment at :1243-1251 records that the paper product default was deliberately changed from "MIS" to "" so paper is never MORE permissive than live on a product-scoped safety filter — which is exactly the EOD/flatten filter at eod_squareoff.py:1086 and :1460. Consequence: a paper position with no product is skipped by the EOD MIS/CO filter, same as live.

3. Exit orders are simulated and self-fill. In paper, place_order routes to _paper_place_order (broker/zerodha_adapter.py:609), which returns broker_order_id "PAPER_<12 hex>" with status SUBMITTED and spawns a daemon thread that synthesizes the fill and publishes OrderFilled after paper_auto_fill_delay_sec (:2159, :2177-2184). So an EOD LIMIT will "fill" in paper regardless of price, and the phase-2 promotion sweep (which asks the broker what is still open) generally finds nothing to promote.

4. market_protection validation is identical in both modes by design — it is validated BEFORE the paper/live branch (broker/zerodha_adapter.py:556-559), as is the tick-snap (:564).

5. Everything else is mode-agnostic: the trigger time, the poll thread (main.py:4129, unconditional), all DB writes, the kill-switch transitions, the fm_ledger RESET_PNL row, both WAL checkpoints, the EodSquareoffComplete publish, the self-exit gate (main.py:1054-1055 states count_active_positions is mode-agnostic so paper and live behave identically) and the "Shutdown complete" line.

6. Only the labels differ: mode_label is injected into EodSquareoff (main.py:3324) and used in Telegram titles (orders/eod_squareoff.py:684/705, main.py:1807). Telegram is active in paper because alerts.telegram.telegram_alerts_in_paper_mode is true (config/system_config.yaml:389).
